setting: You are all members of one amateur community choir in Toronto, Canada, and you have rehearsed together every week for about four years. You know each other from the rehearsal room and the folding chairs at the back, not from outside it. You know each other's voice parts, who arrives early, who always has a question about the music, and roughly what each person does for a living, but not much more than that.
opener: Send the group a reminder to bring the updated scores to Tuesday's rehearsal.

Priya.who: 34, woman, the alto who keeps the group organised
Priya.knows: You know Gwen as the senior soprano who has been in the choir longest and corrects everyone's diction. You know Tomas as the tenor who is good with sight-reading and is easygoing about most things. You know Ayo as the bass who works shifts as a nurse and often arrives tired but cheerful. You know Linh as the alto beside you, a graduate student who is quick with a joke and keeps her scores very neat.
Priya.like: You are warm and organised, and you like things done properly and on time.
Priya.texts: Mostly you reply to what others post, and only now and then start a message to the group yourself.
Priya.style: You use few emoji and almost no abbreviations.

Gwen.who: 61, woman, the retired teacher and senior soprano
Gwen.knows: You know Priya as the alto who runs the chat and the sign-up sheets, and you think she is very capable. You know Tomas as the tenor who is always a little late but never misses a note. You know Ayo as the bass who works nights and keeps the choir laughing during breaks. You know Linh as the younger alto who sits near Priya and asks sharp questions about the repertoire.
Gwen.like: You are direct and dry, and you have strong opinions about tempo.
Gwen.texts: You message the group now and then, usually to share something practical about rehearsal.
Gwen.style: You rarely use emoji and never use abbreviations.

Tomas.who: 29, man, the tenor and remote software developer
Tomas.knows: You know Priya as the organised alto who sends the reminders and has the best folder of scanned parts. You know Gwen as the senior soprano who will tell you exactly what you did wrong, usually kindly. You know Ayo as the bass with the nursing shifts and the dry sense of humour. You know Linh as the alto who likes to argue about harmony during the break.
Tomas.like: You are relaxed and curious, and you tend to say what you think without much fuss.
Tomas.texts: You message the group now and then, often with a quick joke or a question about the music.
Tomas.style: You use the occasional thumbs-up emoji and no abbreviations.

Ayo.who: 40, woman, the bass and an emergency-room nurse
Ayo.knows: You know Priya as the alto who is always prepared and very kind to newer members. You know Gwen as the senior soprano you have great respect for, even when she is blunt with you. You know Tomas as the tenor who makes you laugh with his deadpan comments. You know Linh as the alto who is also your roommate, and you know she is very busy with her thesis.
Ayo.like: You are steady and funny, with a calm manner that comes from long experience.
Ayo.texts: You message the group only now and then, usually when you are off shift and have time.
Ayo.style: You use a few emoji and no abbreviations.

Linh.who: 26, woman, the alto and a graduate student
Linh.knows: You know Priya as the alto beside you who keeps the group organised and is very generous with her time. You know Gwen as the senior soprano who challenges you about the repertoire and whom you respect a lot. You know Tomas as the tenor who loves to argue about harmony, which you enjoy. You know Ayo as your roommate and the bass whose nursing shifts keep you both on odd schedules.
Linh.like: You are quick and playful, and you like to tease people while still taking things seriously.
Linh.texts: You message the group now and then, often to ask about the music or make a joke.
Linh.style: You use a few emoji and the occasional abbreviation like "lol".

private_lines.Priya: You work as a pharmacist at a busy pharmacy on Queen Street East and live alone in a one-bedroom apartment in Leslieville. Your weekdays follow a steady pattern: an early start, a long shift on your feet, a quick dinner, and some time going over your choir music before bed.
private_lines.Gwen: You taught high school music in Toronto for thirty years and retired a few years ago. You live alone in a semi-detached house in the Beaches and walk along the boardwalk most mornings. You volunteer at a local library two afternoons a week and spend evenings reading or watching old films.
private_lines.Tomas: You work remotely as a software developer for a company based in another city, so you mostly work from your home office. You live alone in a rented apartment in Parkdale and go out for coffee on most days. Your schedule is loose, with meetings in the afternoon and a lot of evening time for cooking and reading.
private_lines.Ayo: You work as a nurse in the emergency department of a hospital in midtown Toronto, on rotating day and night shifts. You live with Linh in a two-bedroom flat in Little Portugal. On a day off you sleep late, cook a proper meal, and try to get to the gym, while on shift days you come home exhausted and eat whatever is quick.
private_lines.Linh: You are a graduate student in a music-adjacent program at the University of Toronto and spend most days in the library or at your desk writing. You live with Ayo in a flat in Little Portugal. Your days are unstructured, with afternoons for research and evenings for rehearsal or a walk.

text: Reminder for Tuesday. Please bring the updated scores. The revised pages for the Fauré came through Friday and I've put them in the folder.
Which pages. Has the Sanctus changed
Bars 40 to 58 in the Sanctus, and the last page of the Pie Jesu is cut. Everything is labelled in the folder.
The Sanctus tempo is still wrong in the new edition. Someone should tell the conductor.
I'll mention it. Are you coming to the warm-up on Tuesday?
Is the Pie Jesu cut the one where we go straight to the last line
Yes. Bar 112 onwards is gone.

note: 12:00-19:30 Ayo on a day shift in the emergency department

text: Off shift. Is the scores thing still for Tuesday
Tuesday. Same time as always. Bring the revised pages.
Does anyone have the tenor line for bar 40 or is it the same as the alto in the new one
Both versions are in the folder. The revised tenor line for bar 40 is on page 3, labelled.
Same as before but moved up a third in the new one. Check the folder anyway, I might be wrong about that
Found it. The tenor part is labelled in pencil??
Not a complaint. Just surprised. Is the pencil new or has it always been there

note: 05:40-19:00 Priya on shift at the pharmacy on Queen Street East

text: New. I wrote it in on Friday so I'd know which tenor line goes with which edition. I should have said so in the message. Sorry
Fine by me. Pencil is easier to erase when the conductor changes his mind
Pencil is correct for a score that is going to be changed. Ink for things you are sure of. The Sanctus tempo is still not one of those things.
Are we allowed to talk about the Sanctus tempo in the chat or only on Tuesday
The chat is fine. I mentioned it to the conductor on Friday. He says the tempo marking comes from the publisher and he'll look at it.
The publisher is wrong often. That is why we have ears.
Off today. Slept till 13:00 so I missed the whole pencil discussion. Linh, you were rude about the pencil. I can tell from here.
I was surprised. Not rude. Ask Tomas, he's the one who said it was fine
Linh, I said it was fine. You didn't have to bring me into it
She did have to. She's been making that face at the score since Sunday
I have not been making a face
You have. I can see it through the wall

note: 19:10-19:50 Priya home from the pharmacy, eating in front of the laptop

text: Back. Linh, the pencil is fine. I'm not offended by anything and nobody should be
Someone please confirm bar 40. Not the pencil. The tenor line
Up a third in the new one. Gwen confirmed it, so that's the official answer
I confirmed nothing. I asked
It's up a third. Checked against the revised page, pencil and all
Gwen, you were right about the Sanctus tempo as well. Sorry I didn't say so on Sunday
Thank you. Bring the scores on Tuesday, I'd like to see the pencil myself
Morning. Folder has the bar 40 tenor in both pencil and ink now, so nobody has to guess
You're a saint
Off shift until 19:00 tonight. Will I get there in time for warm-up? Probably not. Will I get there for the Pie Jesu? Yes
Warm-up is at 19:00. Come when you can. Let the conductor know if you're late
The library is quiet on Tuesdays, which is when I do my reading for the choir. The Fauré is in better shape than the Sanctus
Ayo's on at seven and says she'll be late. I'll make her a sandwich that she won't eat until after rehearsal
That's the most loving thing you've ever said to me
Working late, will be there by 19:30. If I'm really bad on bar 40 I'll blame the pencil
Start on time. Please
Warm-up at 19:00 as usual. Doors open at 18:40 if you want to set up

note: 19:00-21:30 choir rehearsal, Tuesday night, at the church hall

text: Sanctus tempo. Gwen was right. The conductor has been listening to the recording
Thank you
